FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Alphabet Object Cards A–Z

Twenty-six objects, one to a card — the apple, the dog, the moon — as bold, flat-colour pictures with no letters beside them. Perfect for guessing games: hide the card, reveal it slowly, and let the guesses run before anyone names it.

THE CARDS

All twenty-six.

Tap any card to open its own page — the full-size card, the words to say together, and the download, print and share buttons.

AppleA is for appleBallB is for ballCatC is for catDogD is for dogElephantE is for elephantFishF is for fishGrapesG is for grapesHouseH is for houseIce creamI is for ice creamJuiceJ is for juiceKiteK is for kiteLionL is for lionMoonM is for moonNestN is for nestOrangeO is for orangePigP is for pigQueenQ is for queenRainbowR is for rainbowSunS is for sunTurtleT is for turtleUmbrellaU is for umbrellaVanV is for vanWhaleW is for whaleXylophoneX is for xylophoneYo-yoY is for yo-yoZebraZ is for zebra
HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Little ways that work.

  1. 01

    Start small

    Pick three cards and lay them face up. Three cards is a lovely little class — the whole alphabet can wait.

  2. 02

    Follow the arrows

    Reveal the card slowly and let the guesses fly. Wrong guesses are the fun part — the naming comes after.

  3. 03

    Tape one up

    Put today’s card at eye level — the fridge, a door. Passing it again and again is quietly powerful practice.

  4. 04

    Match the sets

    Lay a card from this set beside the same card from another letter set and let your child find the pair. The same letter keeps showing up, wearing different clothes.

      FLASHCARD · ALPHABET OBJECT CARDS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Apple Object Card — the Letter A Picture (A is for Apple)

      Just the apple — no letters next to it. Cover the card, reveal it slowly and play “what could this be?” — then say the real word together.

      Say it together

      “A is for apple. Aaa — apple!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the letter, the word, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Guessing first, naming after. Whatever the guess is, take it — “a moon!” “a banana!” — then say the real word together and move on while it is still a game.
